# A ```{typst} block looks like an executable cell to Quarto's engine

engine: markdown

Every figure on this page is compiled by the Typst binary Quarto ships, as the page is built.

## A figure

````markdown
```{typst}
#circle(radius: 1cm, fill: blue)
```
````

```{typst}
#circle(radius: 1cm, fill: blue)
```

## A table

Typst draws the table, and the result arrives as one image:

````markdown
```{typst}
#table(
  columns: 3,
  [*Format*], [*Writer*], [*Figures*],
  [HTML], [html], [image],
  [PDF], [latex], [image],
  [Typst], [typst], [native or image],
)
```
````

```{typst}
#table(
  columns: 3,
  [*Format*], [*Writer*], [*Figures*],
  [HTML], [html], [image],
  [PDF], [latex], [image],
  [Typst], [typst], [native or image],
)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
An image carries no text for a screen reader.
Give a table `alt` text, or write it in Markdown when the data must stay readable.
:::

## Size

`width` and `height` set the page Typst compiles on, and `margin` sets the space around the drawing.
The default page is `auto`, which shrinks to the content:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| width: 8cm
//| height: 3cm
//| margin: 0.5cm
#align(center + horizon)[
  #rect(width: 100%, height: 100%, fill: teal.lighten(70%), radius: 4pt)[
    #align(center + horizon)[A fixed 8cm by 3cm page]
  ]
]
```
````

```{typst}
//| width: 8cm
//| height: 3cm
//| margin: 0.5cm
#align(center + horizon)[
  #rect(width: 100%, height: 100%, fill: teal.lighten(70%), radius: 4pt)[
    #align(center + horizon)[A fixed 8cm by 3cm page]
  ]
]
```

## Format and resolution

This site asks for SVG globally, so the figures stay sharp at any zoom:

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-render:
    format: svg
```

One block can ask for another format.
`dpi` applies to PNG alone:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| format: png
//| dpi: 300
#rect(width: 3cm, height: 1.2cm, fill: orange.lighten(50%), radius: 4pt)
```
````

```{typst}
//| format: png
//| dpi: 300
#rect(width: 3cm, height: 1.2cm, fill: orange.lighten(50%), radius: 4pt)
```

Without a `format`, the extension selects one from the output format.

| Value | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `svg` | HTML and slides, where the figure must stay sharp. |
| `png` | Word, PowerPoint, and any consumer that cannot read SVG. |
| `pdf` | PDF through LaTeX, where a vector figure is wanted. |
| `html` | Semantic markup with MathML maths, in HTML output. It needs Typst 0.15 and falls back to SVG. |

: The four output formats. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[16,84]"}

## Alignment

`align` places the image block on the page:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| align: right
#rect(width: 2cm, height: 1cm, fill: purple.lighten(60%), radius: 4pt)
```
````

```{typst}
//| align: right
#rect(width: 2cm, height: 1cm, fill: purple.lighten(60%), radius: 4pt)
```

`left`, `center`, `right`, and `default` are accepted.

## Showing the source

`echo` puts the Typst beside its output, and `code-fold` tucks it away:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| echo: true
//| code-fold: true
//| code-summary: "The Typst behind this circle"
#circle(radius: 0.6cm, fill: green)
```
````

```{typst}
//| echo: true
//| code-fold: true
//| code-summary: "The Typst behind this circle"
#circle(radius: 0.6cm, fill: green)
```

`echo: fenced` includes the block markers and the option comments, so a reader sees the block exactly as it is written.

Per-block options are written as `//| key: value` at the top of the block, and every one of them can be set globally as a default.
The [Reference](../reference.qmd#per-block-options) lists them all.
